title: Agent Assist
one_liner: Contact-center copilot that refreshes intent, churn, frustration, five flags and a macro suggestion about 100 ms after every customer message across eight concurrent chats.
what_it_does: The page is a three-column support console: a queue of eight chats on the left, the active conversation in the middle, and a copilot panel on the right. The user presses "Run all 8 chats". Eight scripted customers then send five messages each on staggered timers. About 40 messages land over roughly 50 seconds. Each new customer message triggers one judgment over the last six messages plus a customer profile (plan, tenure, prior tickets) and a catalog of 12 macros. The copilot shows the intent, two 0-3 gauges (churn risk, frustration), fired signal chips (needs supervisor, regulatory, refund requested, apologize first, resolvable now), a code-computed "refund eligible" chip, and the suggested macro. If macro confidence is at least 0.6 the macro body is auto-filled into the reply box and auto-sent 1.5 s later; below that the panel lists the top three macros with probabilities for the agent to pick; "none" means reply freehand. Queue rows show badges (escalate, churn, frustrated, regulatory, refund) and re-sort by a priority score so a supervisor sees the hot chats first. A metrics bar shows count judged, browser-measured p50/p95 panel latency, and a speedup versus a 4 s simulated LLM baseline toggle that greys the panel with a countdown.

jev_questions.instructions: Which macro from `catalog_of_macros` is the best canned reply for the agent to send in response to the LAST customer message in `conversation`, given the whole conversation so far? Pick `none` if no macro fits the latest message.
options: duplicate_charge_refund
account_unlock_reset
two_factor_recovery
escalate_to_supervisor
sla_credit
feature_availability_by_plan
feature_request_logged
privacy_data_request
shipping_tracking_update
shipping_replacement
bug_acknowledged_engineering
guided_walkthrough
none
jev_questions.state_shape: {conversation:[{role:'customer'|'agent',text}] (last 6), customer:{plan,tenure_months,prior_tickets}, catalog_of_macros:[{id,title,summary}] x12}; each option criterion is `${title}: ${summary}`; none = 'No macro in the catalog is a good reply to the customer's latest message; the agent should write a custom reply'

jev_questions.instructions: What is the primary intent of the customer in the LAST customer message of `conversation`, in the context of the earlier messages?
options: billing_dispute: A charge, invoice, duplicate payment or refund problem
account_access: Cannot log in, locked out, password or 2FA problems
cancellation_threat: Customer says or implies they will leave, cancel or switch to a competitor
feature_question: Asking whether something is possible, supported, or on the roadmap
data_privacy_request: Requests about personal data: erasure, export, GDPR, CCPA or legal demands
shipping_delay: A physical order is late, lost or stuck in transit
bug_report: Something is broken and the customer describes errors or provides logs
general_help: Needs guidance using the product, confused about the interface
gratitude_or_closing: Thanking the agent, confirming the problem is solved, or ending the chat
other: None of the above

jev_questions.instructions: How likely is this customer to cancel or leave, judging from the whole `conversation` and `customer` profile?
options: 0: No churn signal: the customer is neutral or positive about staying
1: Mild: some dissatisfaction but no mention of leaving
2: Elevated: repeated problems or comparisons with alternatives, leaving is plausible
3: Severe: explicitly threatens to cancel, switch provider, or demands an exit

jev_questions.instructions: How frustrated is the customer in the LAST customer message of `conversation`?
options: 0: Calm and polite
1: Slightly annoyed or impatient
2: Clearly frustrated, repeats complaints or uses emphatic language
3: Angry or hostile, ultimatums, insults or shouting

jev_questions.instructions: Should this chat be escalated to a human supervisor or manager right now, based on the `conversation`?
options: true: The customer explicitly asks for a manager, threatens to leave, raises a legal or regulatory demand, or the issue is beyond what a front-line agent can resolve
false: A front-line agent can handle this conversation on their own

jev_questions.instructions: Does the customer ask for, or clearly expect, money back (a refund, chargeback, reimbursement or credit) anywhere in the `conversation`?
options: true: The customer asks for a refund, reimbursement, or account credit
false: No request or expectation of money back

jev_questions.instructions: Does the `conversation` contain a data-protection or legal request, such as GDPR, CCPA, right to erasure, right of access, data export, subpoena or a demand made under a law or regulation?
options: true: The customer cites a law or regulation, or makes a data erasure, data access or legal demand
false: An ordinary support conversation with no legal or data-protection request

jev_questions.instructions: Should the agent begin the next reply with an apology, because the customer in the `conversation` was harmed or inconvenienced by something on the company's side (a bug, outage, wrong charge, delay or poor prior support)?
options: true: The company caused a problem or inconvenience; the reply should open with an apology
false: Nothing to apologize for: a neutral question, a user-side issue, or the customer is thanking us

jev_questions.instructions: Can the agent most likely fully resolve the customer's issue within this chat session, without waiting on engineering, a carrier, a legal team or a manager?
options: true: The issue can be closed in this chat: answering a question, sending a link, guiding through the UI, or issuing a refund the agent can do
false: Resolution depends on another team, an external party, a multi-day process, or the customer is too upset to close today

request_cadence: One systemOne request per customer message, all nine questions fanned out in that single call. 40 messages per full run over about 50 s, so about 0.8 requests/s, with bursts of 2-3 in the same second across the eight chats. Server semaphore caps in-flight at 8. Single-chat mode fires one request per "Next message" click.

dm1_mapping.notes: Transcript text = last 6 messages rendered as 'Customer: ...\nAgent: ...' lines, with the last customer line prefixed 'LATEST Customer:' so the label descriptions can refer to the latest message. Prepend one line 'Profile: pro plan, 14 months, 2 prior tickets.' Response: label -> answer.choice, probability -> answer.confidence, scores -> answer.probabilities. gateMacro keeps threshold 0.6 unchanged. Build labels once from MACROS at module load.

dm1_mapping.notes: One batched call covers all five flags. Response results[0] -> needs_escalation. Per-statement hints are not possible in one batch because when_true/when_false are shared, so the statements carry the criteria instead. If accuracy on the seeded scripts is poor, split into five single-statement calls with the hints listed below and accept 5 extra requests per message (still within budget when batched across chats). Hints for a split call: when_true 'The customer asks for a manager, threatens to leave, cites a law, or the issue is beyond a front-line agent'; when_false 'A front-line agent can handle this alone'. answer -> noul >= 0.5; probability -> noul.

browser_plan: Rebuild as a Vite/React page at demo.milliseconds.ai/agent-assist with the three-column layout from the original, restyled with the milliseconds site tokens from ~/projects/cloudraker-spring-2026. Copy scripts.ts, macros.ts, store.ts, Queue, Conversation, MetricsBar as-is. Replace server/jev.ts with a thin proxy worker route (POST /api/dm1/:route) that adds the bearer key and forwards to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/:route; the key never reaches the bundle. In the browser, replace judgeMessage with a judge(chat) that fires the five calls per message in parallel (classify best_macro, classify intent, rate churn, rate frustration, yes-no with 5 statements) and merges them into the same JudgeAnswers shape so Copilot and engine.ts stay unchanged. Measure panelMs in the browser around the Promise.all and read x-inference-ms from each response for the server-side badge. Request budget: 40 messages x 5 calls = 200 requests per full run, which over 50 s is 4 req/s, above the 2 req/s target. Fix with a client-side batcher: a 250 ms window collects pending judgments from all chats, then sends one request per route with texts:[...] (up to 32, one per pending chat) so bursts from concurrent chats collapse into 5 requests per tick, and a token-bucket caps outgoing requests at 2/s. Worst case is then 5 requests per 250 ms window only when chats collide, and a full run stays near 100-150 requests. Show the x-inference-ms and per-message panel latency exactly as the original. On HTTP 429 or 5xx: retry once after the Retry-After or 1 s, mark the chat row with a "rate limited, retrying" pill, and if it fails again keep the previous judgment visible and show an error chip; never block the script timers. Keep the 4 s simulated-LLM baseline toggle and the copy that says it is artificial. Drop MOCK mode.
risks: Jev returned all nine answers in one call; dm1 needs five calls per message. Latency shown will be the max of the five, likely 150-400 ms, so the '~100 ms' README claim will not hold; measure and print real numbers.
The five yes/no statements share when_true/when_false in a batch, so the batch form loses per-flag hints. Eval on the seeded scripts first; fall back to five separate calls if flags misfire.

Jev questions reference the JSON state (`catalog_of_macros`, `customer` profile) directly; dm1 only sees text. The transcript rendering plus a one-line profile prefix must carry that context, and best_macro depends on label descriptions alone.
The 'none' macro and gratitude/closing turns are the weakest case for classify; the original's 0.6 auto-fill gate may need tuning against dm1 confidence values.
Rate limit is org-wide across all visitors; two people running the demo at once double the request rate, so the throttle must stay conservative and 429 handling must be visible.
rate returns a 0..1 score; mapping to the 0..3 gauge is score*3, which can differ from Jev's expected-value score and shift the CHURN_ALERT badge threshold.
